title: Inference Platform Economics — Fireworks, Together, Baseten, Modal, Replicate, Anyscale

questions.question: Which pricing branch does cost_per_day use for Replicate?
questions.explanation: Replicate is the only local vendor with per_prediction set, so cost_per_day multiplies $0.006 by the prediction count.

questions.question: Baseten serves 100M tokens/day at 900k tokens/minute. Why does the demo still bill 1,440 minutes?
options: The token rate is ignored for per-minute vendors
Baseten bills every request for 60 minutes
The workload is converted to 1,440 predictions
questions.explanation: cost_per_day takes max(saturated_minutes, min_reserved_minutes_per_day); 100M/900k is about 111 minutes, so Baseten's 1,440-minute floor wins.

questions.question: At 500,000 predictions/day, what does Replicate's $0.006 per-prediction field contribute?
questions.explanation: The prediction branch computes 500,000 × $0.006, which is $3,000/day before any separate token comparison.

questions.question: For Fireworks at 100M output tokens/day, which expression is the local per-token cost?
questions.explanation: Fireworks stores $0.90 per million output tokens, and cost_per_day divides tokens by 1e6 before multiplying by that rate.

questions.question: Which vendor has the shortest cold_start_sec in VENDORS?
questions.explanation: The Fireworks row sets cold_start_sec to 1.5, lower than Together 2.0, Modal 2.5, and Replicate 4.0.

questions.question: What utilization rule does the demo give for reserved per-minute billing?
options: Per-minute always wins, even at one request
The pricing model cannot be compared after normalization
questions.explanation: The printed rule of thumb accounts for the reserved-minute floor: per-minute vendors become attractive only when GPU saturation is sustained around 60–70% or more.
